title: Understanding Monetary Policy: Student Awareness, Perceptions, and Financial Behaviors in the Philippine Context
authors: Atento, R. G.; Espelita, C. A. M.; Rao, L.; Tian, Y.
tldr: Filipino students show moderate monetary policy awareness, positively associated with saving and investment behaviors (R²=.22 and R²=.15) but not spending behavior.
problem_and_motivation: Monetary policy awareness affects financial behaviors, but the relationship between knowledge, perceptions, and financial actions in the Philippine student context is underexplored.
approach: Descriptive-correlational survey with 200 respondents across senior high, undergraduate, and graduate levels in Philippine institutions.
Measures monetary policy awareness, perceptions of effectiveness, and financial behaviors.
Correlation and regression analysis guided by Theory of Reasoned Action and Theory of Planned Behavior.
findings: Overall awareness of monetary policy is moderate; graduate and business/economics students show higher understanding.
Awareness positively associated with saving behavior (r=0.31, p<.001) and investment behavior (r=0.24, p=.001).
No significant relationship between awareness and spending behavior.
Awareness and perceptions predict saving (R²=.22) and investment (R²=.15) but not spending (R²=.04).

definitions.definition: Understanding of central bank policies regarding inflation, interest rates, and economic stability.

topics.name: Filipino Young Professionals as a Demographic

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Establishes empirical links between monetary policy awareness and financial behaviors among Filipino students. Confirms knowledge shapes attitudes and influences saving and investment but not spending.
directly_justifies: Monetary policy awareness predicts saving behavior (R²=.22).
Monetary policy awareness predicts investment behavior (R²=.15).
limits: Sample limited to selected Philippine institutions.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 domains. Flagged 1.A, 1.C (high). Rejected algorithmic topics and topic-specific domains as this is a survey-based behavioral economics study.

limitations: Limited to 200 students from selected Philippine institutions.
Cross-sectional design cannot establish causal relationships. [unacknowledged]
